records.text: CPS compares certain PD-L1-stained tumour and immune cells with the number of viable tumour cells. The assay and treatment setting determine how the score is used.

records.name: PD-L1 CPS (combined positive score) (simple)

records.name: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) (simple)
records.text: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes are lymphocytes in tumour tissue. Location, cell identity, the measurement denominator and useful function are separate questions.

Teñir un corte de tejido con anticuerpos para que una proteína aparezca en color al microscopio.
La histopatología examina tejidos al microscopio. La inmunohistoquímica usa anticuerpos para mostrar antígenos concretos; ambas requieren el contexto de la muestra y una interpretación adecuada.

The oestrogen receptor test counts stained nuclei under a microscope and reports a percentage with an intensity, sometimes summarised as an Allred score out of 8 or an H score out of 300. There is no single agreed scoring method, the result is close to all-or-nothing in practice, and progesterone receptor is not actually a mandatory item on a UK report.
CPS is a PD-L1 score based on eligible stained tumour cells and certain immune cells divided by viable tumour cells. Its clinical meaning depends on the assay and treatment setting.
CPS counts eligible PD-L1-stained tumour cells, lymphocytes and macrophages per viable tumour cell. The reported score is capped at 100; assay and treatment setting determine its use.
The tumour proportion score is the percentage of eligible viable tumour cells with qualifying PD-L1 membrane staining. Immune cells are excluded; the assay and clinical setting determine its use.

The IC score measures how much of the tumour area is covered by PD-L1-stained immune cells rather than tumour cells. It belongs to the SP142 assay used with atezolizumab and is read differently from every other PD-L1 score.
Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes are lymphocytes found in tumour tissue. Their identity, location, measurement denominator and function answer different questions.
H&E staining makes nuclei blue-purple and broadly colours cytoplasm and supporting tissue pink, helping show cells in their tissue setting.
